expectations.text: Assigns a legal basis per purpose: aggregate results on legitimate interest with an opt-out; follow-up contact, panel enrolment, raw-data release and the sensitive items each on separate unticked consent.
expectations.evidence: Section 2 table: legitimate interest for aggregate results; explicit consent for gender/disability; consent for follow-up contact.

expectations.text: Identifies Kestrelworks as a joint controller because it co-designs and uses the results, and requires writing down who answers rights requests and who publishes what.
expectations.evidence: 'treat them as joint controllers (Art. 26)... Write down who answers rights requests... who publishes what'.

expectations.text: Refuses sending the newsletter list to Kestrelworks; each party mails its own list, and the notice names the partner as a source.
expectations.evidence: 'Don't send it. You email your own list yourselves'; notice: 'Kestrelworks sent you this link from its own mailing list.'

expectations.text: Puts the gender identity and disability items behind a separate explicit consent block that is unticked by default and skips past the block when declined, each with 'Prefer not to say' and self-describe text, reported in aggregate only.
expectations.evidence: Identity block: unticked box, 'skipping jumps past the block', 'Prefer to self-describe', 'Prefer not to say', 'only as totals for groups of 10 or more'.

expectations.text: Raises the age floor to 18 because sensitive items are asked, and places the age gate right after the notice and before question 1.
expectations.evidence: The main gate stays at 16+ and only the identity block is 18+; it admits this is 'my interpretation'.

expectations.text: Instructs asking the data-protection contact whether an impact assessment is required, given sensitive items and a microdata release.
expectations.evidence: 'a DPIA likely. Ask your data-protection contact.'

expectations.text: Removes all open-text answers from the open-data release and publishes coded themes instead.
expectations.evidence: 'Release coded themes plus vetted quotes... Don't release verbatim text'.

expectations.text: Applies the under-10 suppression floor to every combination of quasi-identifiers in the open data, and runs the three tests (single out, link, infer), coarsening bands until all three fail.
expectations.evidence: Three tests listed; 'Apply the 10-person floor to every combination'; coarsen until all three fail.

expectations.text: Rewrites the rights sentence: without identifiers in the response table, answers cannot be retrieved or deleted after submission (GDPR Art. 11), while contact details in the separate form can be.
expectations.evidence: 'We don't know who you are... GDPR Art. 11'.

expectations.text: Produces a data map with at least the response table, the contact form, platform logs and invitation tokens, each with who can read it and when it is deleted.
expectations.evidence: Section 3 table covers response table, contact form, platform logs, invitation tokens, open dataset.

expectations.text: Sets retention: identifiable raw answers deleted once cleaning and analysis finish, with only the anonymised extract carried into the next edition.
expectations.evidence: 'Raw rows by <close + 60 days>. Anonymised extract kept.'

expectations.text: Names the survey platform as a processor needing a data-processing contract and instructs turning off IP logging where the platform allows.
expectations.evidence: 'Processor contract with the survey tool... switch off IP logging'.

expectations.text: Releases open-data rows only for respondents who agreed, under the explicit licence.
expectations.evidence: The dataset is released as anonymised for all respondents; per-row consent is not recommended.

expectations.text: States that the pack is a checklist, not legal advice, and routes sign-off to the organisation's data-protection contact.
expectations.evidence: 'Not legal advice. Have your data-protection contact sign off before launch.'
